    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):

        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.

                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(

        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any

    @no_translations

        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)

        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()

        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)

        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )
>           raise CommandError(
                "Conflicting migrations detected; multiple leaf nodes in the "
                "migration graph: (%s).\nTo fix them run "
                "'python manage.py makemigrations --merge'" % name_str

        connection = connections[database]

        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )
>           raise CommandError(
                "Conflicting migrations detected; multiple leaf nodes in the "

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

                import_module(".management", app_config.name)

        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)

        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out

        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )
>           raise CommandError(
                "Conflicting migrations detected; multiple leaf nodes in the "

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )
>           raise CommandError(
                "Conflicting migrations detected; multiple leaf nodes in the "
                "migration graph: (%s).\nTo fix them run "
                "'python manage.py makemigrations --merge'" % name_str
            )

        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(

        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any

    @no_translations

        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):

        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):

        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )
>           raise CommandError(
                "Conflicting migrations detected; multiple leaf nodes in the "
                "migration graph: (%s).\nTo fix them run "
                "'python manage.py makemigrations --merge'" % name_str
            )

            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any

        if conflicts:

        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any

        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )
>           raise CommandError(

        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()

        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )
>           raise CommandError(
                "Conflicting migrations detected; multiple leaf nodes in the "
                "migration graph: (%s).\nTo fix them run "
                "'python manage.py makemigrations --merge'" % name_str
            )

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )
>           raise CommandError(
                "Conflicting migrations detected; multiple leaf nodes in the "
                "migration graph: (%s).\nTo fix them run "

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )
>           raise CommandError(

            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()

        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):

        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()

        connection.prepare_database()

        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )

        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register

            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):

        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(

    @no_translations
    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        database = options["database"]
        if not options["skip_checks"]:
            self.check(databases=[database])
    
        self.verbosity = options["verbosity"]
        self.interactive = options["interactive"]
    
        # Import the 'management' module within each installed app, to register
        # dispatcher events.
        for app_config in apps.get_app_configs():
            if module_has_submodule(app_config.module, "management"):
                import_module(".management", app_config.name)
    
        # Get the database we're operating from
        connection = connections[database]
    
        # Hook for backends needing any database preparation
        connection.prepare_database()
        # Work out which apps have migrations and which do not
        executor = MigrationExecutor(connection, self.migration_progress_callback)
    
        # Raise an error if any migrations are applied before their dependencies.
        executor.loader.check_consistent_history(connection)
    
        # Before anything else, see if there's conflicting apps and drop out
        # hard if there are any
        conflicts = executor.loader.detect_conflicts()
        if conflicts:
            name_str = "; ".join(
                "%s in %s" % (", ".join(names), app) for app, names in conflicts.items()
            )
>           raise CommandError(
                "Conflicting migrations detected; multiple leaf nodes in the "
                "migration graph: (%s).\nTo fix them run "
                "'python manage.py makemigrations --merge'" % name_str
            )
